item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00157","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C19","C09","C22"],"selected_candidate_label":"C19","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C19 is a clear material drafting precursor. Both letters address the same recipients, request congressional authorization for a $12 million United States contribution to the same United Nations children's fund for the current fiscal year, explain that the prior authorization expired on June 30, cite the General Assembly's extension of the fund, summarize its humanitarian work and shift toward less-developed regions, and close by urging prompt congressional action. The child updates C19 after the requested legislation passed the Senate but remained pending in the House and adds authorization for fiscal year 1953. C09 is a weaker but relevant template for requesting a quantified U.S. contribution to a United Nations relief program; C22 shares support for U.N. financial obligations but lacks the child's specific structure and target.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I am writing to urge that the Congress complete action on legislation to authorize a United States contribution of $12 million to the United Nations Children's Emergency fund for fiscal year 1952.","parent_excerpt":"I am writing to ask that the Congress authorize a contribution of twelve million dollars by the United States to the International Children's Emergency Fund. This sum would be authorized for the current fiscal year.","explanation":"Nearly identical opening request, amount, contributor, recipient fund, and fiscal-year framing."},{"child_excerpt":"the General Assembly of the United Nations voted more than a year ago to extend the operation of the Children's fund through December, 1953. For that reason, when the authorization for United States contributions to the fund expired last June 30, I requested authorization of a contribution for the current fiscal year.","parent_excerpt":"The General Assembly of the United Nations, on December 1, 1950, extended the operations of the Children's Fund for a period of three years. Since the authorization to make financial contributions to the Fund expired last June 30, we can now make no further contribution without this new authority from the Congress.","explanation":"The same factual and legal predicate appears in the same sequence: General Assembly extension, expiration on June 30, and need for renewed congressional authority."},{"child_excerpt":"The fund is now placing emphasis on work in the less developed countries, primarily to help them establish permanent programs to aid their children.","parent_excerpt":"The main work of the Fund has now shifted from Europe to the underdeveloped areas of Asia and Latin America. Here the Fund will bring supplies and services to help meet urgent needs of children and to strengthen the permanent child welfare programs of the countries themselves.","explanation":"Both use the same substantive justification: the fund's shift toward less-developed countries, combining urgent assistance with durable national child-welfare programs."},{"child_excerpt":"I am confident the people of this country will want to take full advantage of that opportunity. I urge the Congress to act on these authorizations without delay.","parent_excerpt":"I am confident that the people of this country want to continue to support the great work the Fund is doing. It is my hope that the Congress will find it possible to give early consideration to this measure.","explanation":"Closely parallel closing appeal asserting public support and requesting prompt congressional action."}]}
